subject: AI & Agents
title: AI Safety Research
description: A quick, practical guide to AI Safety Research.

hook.text: A research lab's mission: make sure AI doesn't accidentally destroy humanity. No pressure.

buildup.text: AI safety studies alignment — making sure AI systems do what humans actually want.

discovery.text: Key problems include reward hacking, goal misalignment, and power-seeking behavior.

twist.text: We don't know how to verify that a superintelligent system is truly aligned. Not yet.

climax.text: Organizations like MIRI, Anthropic, and DeepMind dedicate teams to these existential questions.

punchline.text: The most important engineering problem: make sure AI wants what we want.

quiz.question: What is the core problem AI safety research addresses?
options: Ensuring AI systems are aligned with human intentions

details.summary: AI safety research works to ensure powerful AI systems behave as intended and align with human values. This includes preventing harmful outputs, maintaining human control, and avoiding catastrophic failures.
details.whyItMatters: As AI becomes more capable, the consequences of misalignment grow more severe. Safety research is the field's attempt to ensure advanced AI remains beneficial and controllable.
takeaways: AI safety prevents harmful behavior and ensures human control
Research areas include alignment, robustness, and interpretability
Investment in safety lags behind investment in AI capabilities

faq.question: What are the main areas of AI safety research?
faq.answer: Key areas include alignment (ensuring AI goals match human values), robustness (reliable behavior in unexpected situations), interpretability (understanding model decisions), and governance frameworks.

faq.question: Is enough being invested in AI safety research?
faq.answer: Most experts say no. Capabilities research receives far more funding than safety work. Several organizations including Anthropic and the AI Safety Institute are working to close the gap.
